1: # Tasks: enforce the conclusion-over-graph tool contract
2: 
3: ## 1. Inventory and classify the tool surface
4: - [x] Enumerate every tool name in `TOOL_DEFINITIONS` (`src/cli/commands/mcp.ts:138+`) and its
5:       dispatch branch (`src/core/services/tool-dispatch.ts:99-286` — note: dispatch lives at
6:       `src/core/services/tool-dispatch.ts`, not under `mcp-handlers/`).
7: - [x] For each, record its return shape (read the handler's return statement) and tag it
8:       `conclusion` or `explicit-topology`.
9:       → verified: audit of all 50 dispatched handlers found only `get_subgraph` emits a raw
10:       `nodes[]`+`edges[]` dump. `get_call_graph` currently returns bounded summary lists but is kept
11:       `explicit-topology` (it is the designated graph-level tool); everything else is `conclusion`
12:       and already compliant — zero existing handler outputs change.
13: - [x] Write the classification table into `src/core/services/mcp-handlers/tool-contract.ts` as a
14:       typed constant `TOOL_OUTPUT_CLASS: Record<string, 'conclusion' | 'explicit-topology'>`.
15:       → verified: completeness test asserts every registered tool name has an entry and there are no
16:       stale entries.
17: 
18: ## 2. Define the contract predicate
19: - [x] In the same module, add `assertConclusionShape(toolName, response)` that, for `conclusion`
20:       tools, checks: (a) no top-level array of id-reference edge objects (`{from,to}` /
21:       `{callerId,calleeId}` / `{source,target}`) larger than `MAX_PROVENANCE_EDGES = 25`, and
22:       (b) no top-level `nodes[]`+`edges[]` pair requiring a join. Resolved `{caller,callee}`
23:       name-pairs are intentionally NOT flagged — they are self-describing conclusions (e.g.
24:       `structural_diff`'s changelog), documented as the boundary in the module.
25:       → verified: throws on a hand-built graph-dump; passes on path/list/metric responses.
26: - [x] Keep the bound a named constant in `src/constants.ts` so it is tunable in one place.
27: 
28: ## 3. Regression test across the live surface
29: - [x] Add `src/core/services/mcp-handlers/tool-contract.test.ts`.
30:       → DEVIATION: the test does NOT invoke handlers against the `.openlore/analysis` fixture —
31:       that directory is gitignored and unavailable in CI, so a fixture-invoking test would be
32:       green locally but broken/skipped in CI. Instead the test is synthetic and deterministic: it
33:       cross-checks `TOOL_OUTPUT_CLASS` against the exported `TOOL_DEFINITIONS` (the real regression
34:       guard for an unclassified new tool) and exercises `assertConclusionShape` against hand-built
35:       conclusion/graph-dump shapes.
36:       → verified: `vitest run src/core/services/mcp-handlers/tool-contract.test.ts` passes (14 tests).
37: - [x] Confirmed this is a plain `.test.ts` (not `.integration.test.ts`) so CI enforces it.
38: 
39: ## 4. Author rule in the spec
40: - [x] Added the `ToolsReturnConclusionsNotGraphs` requirement in `specs/mcp-quality/spec.md`.
41: - [x] Added a one-line note to `CLAUDE.md`'s MCP table area pointing at the contract module.
42: 
43: ## 5. Close the loop
44: - [x] Run `check_spec_drift` for `mcp-quality` after implementation.
45: - [x] `record_decision` titled "MCP conclusion-over-graph output contract" recorded (id `4b88176d`)
46:       with the two explicit-topology exceptions named in consequences.
